title: Post Basic Diploma in Specialty Nursing
kicker: One-year specialty training for registered nurses

value.body: The Indian Nursing Council (INC) prescribes post basic diploma programmes that let registered nurses specialise in one clinical area, such as critical care, cardio-thoracic, oncology, operation room, emergency and disaster, neonatal, psychiatric or neuroscience nursing. They are run by INC-recognised nursing colleges and hospitals, and training is largely clinical, on the wards and units of that speciality.

items.label: Course length
items.source: INC post basic diploma syllabi (as reported)

items.label: Who can apply
items.note: Registered as a nurse and midwife (RN & RM) with a State Nursing Council

items.label: Experience asked
items.note: Clinical experience after registration; the requirement varies by speciality and institution
items.source: INC post basic diploma syllabi (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Hold a GNM diploma or B.Sc Nursing, register with your State Nursing Council and gain the clinical experience the course asks for. Apply to an institution recognised by INC for that speciality; selection is through the institution's own entrance test and interview, or a merit list. Check INC's list of recognised institutions before applying.

value.title: At a glance
items: It is a diploma, not a degree, so posts and courses that ask for a nursing degree still need a B.Sc or Post Basic B.Sc Nursing.
Seats are few and are mostly in larger hospitals and nursing colleges.
Some government hospitals depute their in-service nurses to these courses; rules differ by state.
The speciality chosen shapes later work, such as ICU, operation theatre or neonatal units.
